figures.alt: Illustration of a girl in a dim classroom shining a flashlight so the beam crosses the room to a friend at her desk.
figures.caption: A flashlight beam is a pattern of light that can carry a message across a room.

figures.alt: Photo of a drum with a pile of rice grains and a wooden spoon resting on the drum skin.
figures.caption: Set up before the test: rice on the drum skin. Tap the drum skin gently and watch the rice.

figures.alt: Four rows. In each, a flashlight on the left sends a beam to a material. Clear plastic: the light passes straight through. Wax paper: some light passes through and spreads out, so it is blurry. Cardboard: the light is blocked and there is a shadow behind it. Mirror: the light bounces back toward the flashlight.
figures.caption: What a beam of light does to four materials: passes through, spreads, is blocked, or bounces.
